title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature reliance through controlled suppression

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2 Experiment II: Domain-specific Feature Reliance (RS and MI paragraphs)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 5.2's dataset lists contradict the paper's own Figure 4 caption. For remote sensing, the prose states 'Figure 4g–i reports suppression curves for five very-high-resolution RGB datasets: UCMerced [61], RSD46-WHU [62], DeepGlobe [63], PatternNet [64], and AID [65]', but the Figure 4 caption lists the datasets plotted in panels g–i as AID, EuroSAT, NWPU, RESISC45, and UC Merced. RSD46-WHU, DeepGlobe, and PatternNet appear only in the prose/reference list while EuroSAT, NWPU, and RESISC45 appear only in the figure (and are not cited anywhere in the reference list). For medical imaging, the text describes results for 'PathMNIST and BloodMNIST', 'RetinaMNIST and DermaMNIST', and 'ChestMNIST', but Figure 4 panels d–f plot BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, and PathMNIST: RetinaMNIST and ChestMNIST are discussed but not plotted, while BreastMNIST and OCTMNIST are plotted but never discussed. A reader cannot map the prose's reported suppression curves onto the datasets actually displayed, undermining traceability of the central domain-comparison claims (MI relies on color, RS relies on texture).

Figure 4's panel dataset lists conflict with Section 5.2's prose and the paper's own reference list. The RS panels (g-i) plot AID, EuroSAT, NWPU, RESISC45, and UC Merced, but the prose names UCMerced [61], RSD46-WHU [62], DeepGlobe [63], PatternNet [64], and AID [65]; three of the plotted RS datasets (EuroSAT, NWPU, RESISC45) have no citation in the reference list. The MI panels (d-f) plot BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, PathMNIST, while the prose discusses PathMNIST, BloodMNIST, RetinaMNIST, DermaMNIST, and ChestMNIST - two datasets are discussed but not plotted and two are plotted but never discussed. This figure-text mismatch affects the paper's core cross-domain experiment.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification of 'ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture' (NeurIPS 2025 oral, arXiv:2509.20234). 20 snippets were segmented; 7 escalated for specialist review (uncertainty >= 0.30), plus a full-paper cross-section consistency pass. The paper's core numerical claims are internally consistent: all percentages in Section 5.1 (80%/83%/28%/76%/62%/65%) match Table 3 exactly, the prose metric values in Section 4.1 match Table 2 within rounding, and the harmonic-mean composites in Table 2 deviate only by minor rounding (0.004-0.015), well within tolerance. Web-verified citations [8], [13], [19], [22], [33], [18] are real and substantively accurate; the GitHub code repository exists and matches the paper; no novelty over-claim was found. The paper is macro-level consistent (Abstract, Method, Results, Conclusion all align). Two related findings were confirmed: (1) Section 5.2's dataset lists contradict Figure 4's caption - the RS prose names UCMerced/RSD46-WHU/DeepGlobe/PatternNet/AID while the figure plots EuroSAT/NWPU/RESISC45/UC Merced/AID, and the MI prose discusses RetinaMNIST/ChestMNIST which are not among the plotted MedMNIST datasets (BreastMNIST/OCTMNIST are plotted but never discussed); three plotted RS datasets have no citation. This figure-text mismatch undermines traceability of the central domain-comparison experiment. Both findings are medium-confidence data-consistency issues, not fatal statistical or methodological errors, so the paper warrants review but not correction.
